business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail of Dietary Supplements and Nutraceuticals Online

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (based on French Napoleonic codes and Luxembourg statutory codes; EU law directly applicable; no common law doctrine of binding precedent)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Belgium-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU) bilateral investment treaty network with approximately 90 third states
Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union - free movement of capital and establishment within EU internal market
Energy Charter Treaty (Luxembourg is a Contracting Party)
EU-China Comprehensive Agreement on Investment (signed 30 December 2020; ratification pending)
China-Luxembourg Double Taxation Agreement (1994 Convention, as amended by Protocol of 9 October 2009)
Luxembourg-United States DTA (1996 Convention, as amended) and FATCA Intergovernmental Agreement

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies as amended (SARL formation, minimum capital EUR 12,000, 25% paid-up rule); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies as amended (RCS registration and name reservation); Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing as amended (Luxembourg AML/CFT cornerstone statute); Law of 13 January 2019 creating the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), Mem. A No. 15 of 21 January 2019; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 28 February 2019 on RBE filing formalities; CSSF Regulation No 12-02 of 14 December 2012 on AML/CFT as amended by CSSF Regulation No 20-05; Law of 19 December 2020 on asset freezing and sectoral prohibitions in the fight against terrorist financing; Criminal Code Articles 506-1 et seq.; CJEU Joined Cases C-37/20 and C-601/20, judgment of 22 November 2022 limiting general public access to UBO registers
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (general public access suspended following CJEU judgment of 22 November 2022; access granted to Luxembourg supervisory authorities, the Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF), notaries, lawyers, and other obliged entities for CDD purposes; third parties may apply to obtain limited access upon proof of a legitimate interest)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Extract of the Company Register / Certificate of Incorporation (Certificate of Good Standing) of each corporate shareholder and corporate UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Competent companies registry or registrar of companies in the state of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille by the competent authority of the issuing state; if the issuing state is not party to the 1961 Hague Apostille Convention, full consular legalization by the Luxembourg Embassy or Consulate is required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good conduct / criminal record extract (casier judiciaire) of each proposed manager, director, and authorized signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice, national police, or other competent criminal-record authority of the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization where the Hague Convention is inapplicable); must be translated into French by a sworn translator if issued in another language

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Power of Attorney (procuration notariée) granted by each shareholder in favor of the Luxembourg notary or incorporation agent for the execution of the notarial deed and ancillary filings
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public in the home jurisdiction of each shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or consular legalization; notarially certified French translation required for Luxembourg notarial use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Passport / national identity card copies of all individuals identified as UBOs, managers, and authorized signatories (individualized and notarially certified)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary public of the home state, issuing government authority, or competent consulate/embassy
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Apostille not generally required where copy is certified by the issuing authority or a notary; notarial certification in Luxembourg-compliant form and French translation required

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter and confirmation of source of funds / source of wealth for the EUR 12,000 share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Account-holding bank or credit institution of each contributing shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: No apostille required; original signed letter on bank letterhead, subject to independent verification by the Luxembourg credit institution and AML/CFT team

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening against the OFAC SDN List, EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List, UN Security Council Consolidated Lists, and Luxembourg national asset-freezing measures under the Law of 19 December 2020. PEP status defined per FATF Recommendation 12 and Article 3(9) of Directive (EU) 2015/849 as amended: enhanced due diligence (EDD) is mandatory for foreign PEPs, domestic prominent public functions assessed on risk, and UBOs connected to PEPs. High-risk third countries per FATF and EU delegated regulations trigger additional EDD measures: verified UBO identity, source of wealth, source of funds, business rationale, and ongoing automated transaction monitoring. CDD is performed at inception and continuously throughout the business relationship; any suspicion of money laundering or terrorist financing is reportable without delay to the Luxembourg Financial Intelligence Unit (CRF).

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), operator of the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS) - official portal lbr.lu; pre-incorporation name reservation is filed electronically via RCS e-forms and myGuichet.lu (guichet.public.lu), legally anchored in the Law of 19 December 2002 on the RCS as amended
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be written in Latin script and in one of the three administrative languages (Luxembourgish, French, or German). Non-Roman scripts (including Chinese characters and Cyrillic) are not accepted; only a transliterated Latin-script version is registrable. The name must be distinguishable from all existing registered names and must not mislead the public as to the legal form, object, or solvency of the entity; for a SARL the suffix 'SARL' or the phrase 'Societe a Responsabilite Limitee' is customarily included in the corporate name.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Societe de participation financiere (requires regulatory confirmation for SOPARFI status)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Extension: the applicant may refile the reservation application before expiry for one additional 30-day term; any further extension requires written justification and is subject to renewed distinctiveness and availability screening. Rejection SOP: the LBR registrar issues a written refusal identifying the conflicting or prohibited element; the applicant may (1) refile with a corrected or modified name, (2) submit a notarial consent or waiver letter from the holder of the conflicting name, or (3) lodge a judicial appeal by petition (requete) before the commercial chamber of the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg within 15 days of notification of the refusal.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Conditionally permissible. Under the Law of 10 August 1915, a SARL must have a registered office ('siege social') situated in the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, being a real, identified place capable of receiving service of process and where statutory corporate records are accessible. A commercial domiciliation company providing a full administrative address satisfies the bare registration requirement. However, for a high-risk cross-border nutraceuticals e-commerce SARL (ISIC 4791), a pure virtual-postbox model is not commercially viable: a physical operating substance is expected for the mandatory establishment authorisation under the Law of 2 September 2011, the Ministry of Health food-supplement market-access notification, VAT registration, and the required high-risk merchant account. A hybrid model (domiciliation address plus local substance arrangement with staff, records, and management oversight) is strongly recommended.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk: 25-30% within the first 24 months for this high-risk e-commerce profile; the probability rises to approximately 40% if a pure virtual office or nominee directors are used. Unannounced on-site inspections may be conducted by the Luxembourg customs and excise administration (for goods compliance), the labour inspectorate ITM (for employment and physical presence indicators), and the competent food-supplement health authority (market-access and product-safety checks). Credit institutions and acquiring banks will also independently commission physical-visit verification of the registered office and operational substance before onboarding.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies, as amended (the '1915 Law'), Articles 710-1 to 710-24 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Commercial and Companies Register, as amended; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) regulations on electronic incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) of the Luxembourg District Court (Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Acte constitutif (Articles of Incorporation) together with the RCS registration declaration (déclaration en vue de l'immatriculation)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum share capital EUR 12,000, fully subscribed and fully paid up at formation. Cash contributions must be deposited into a blocked escrow account (compte bloqué) opened in the name of the company-in-formation with a Luxembourg credit institution; funds are released only upon RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a registered auditor's valuation report (rapport du réviseur d'entreprises).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, by unanimous consent, that the subscriptions set out in the share subscription schedule are accepted and that the paid-in share capital of EUR 12,000 is allotted in accordance with the articles of incorporation; RESOLVED that the registered office of the company is fixed at [●] street, L-● Luxembourg, Grand Duchy of Luxembourg, and that all statutory mail shall be kept at that address; FURTHER RESOLVED that [●] is appointed as gérant (manager) with sole signature authority, that [●] is designated as AML compliance officer, and that the mandates for opening the corporate bank account, filing the RCS registration, and publishing in RESA are ratified; such appointments take immediate effect.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and legalization of the articles of incorporation (statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (required where the contribution comprises real property); otherwise the founders by private deed under the 2016 reform; electronic filing portal of Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the draft statutes in French or German, including corporate name, registered office address, corporate object limited to online retail of dietary supplements and nutraceuticals, share capital of EUR 12,000, and the appointment of the gérant. Where an in-kind real-estate contribution exists, execute the deed before a Luxembourg notary; otherwise execute the private deed and arrange qualified electronic signatures. Attach criminal record certificates and declarations of non-bankruptcy for each proposed manager.
required_dossiers: Draft articles of incorporation (projet de statuts)
Valid identity documents (passport or national ID) of all founders and managers
Criminal record certificate (extrait du casier judiciaire) for each manager
Written acceptance of office by each gérant
Power of attorney where a founder acts through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the registration file is queried or returned, promptly amend the statutory provisions or supporting declarations and resubmit to the notary or LBR within the prescribed cure period; obtain a formal regularization opinion from the notary to preserve the incorporation timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Opening of the blocked capital escrow account and deposit of share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a blocked account (compte bloqué) in the name of the company-in-formation, deposit EUR 12,000 from the founders' funds, and obtain a blocking certificate (attestation de blocage) from the bank. Instruct the bank that the funds are releasable only upon presentation of the RCS registration certificate or notarial confirmation. This certificate is annexed to the incorporation filing submitted to the notary or LBR.
required_dossiers: Signed or notarized draft articles of incorporation
KYC documentation for all shareholders and ultimate beneficial owners
Source-of-funds and source-of-wealth evidence for the EUR 12,000
AML questionnaire reflecting the high-risk nutraceuticals e-commerce profile
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond to enhanced due diligence queries with supplementary source-of-funds documentation; if the initial bank declines the file, apply to an alternative CSSF-regulated institution or use the notary's escrow facility to hold the subscribed capital pending registration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Filing of the incorporation dossier with the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed articles of incorporation and the RCS registration declaration (déclaration en vue de l'immatriculation) through the LBR e-filing portal or via the notary's electronic relay. Attach the capital blocking certificate, the gérant consent and specimen signatures, and proof of the registered office address. Pay the registration fee online and request simultaneous publication in RESA.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of incorporation
RCS registration declaration form
Bank blocking certificate or notarial statement confirming paid-up capital
Gérant consent, identity proof, and specimen signatures
Registered office confirmation and, if applicable, landlord authorization
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Where the RCS registrar issues a formal request for correction, remedy by filing a supplementary declaration within the statutory deadline; ensure alignment with the 1915 Law before refiling; in case of refusal, petition the President of the Luxembourg District Court.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in RESA and issuance of the certified RCS extract
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon RCS registration, the register automatically publishes an extract of the incorporation in RESA. Download the certified extract (extrait du registre) and the RCS registration number, verify the accuracy of the published particulars, and circulate the certified extract to founders and managers as definitive evidence of legal personality.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number and certified extract
RESA publication confirmation in PDF form
Notification letters to founders, managers, and the appointed bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RESA publication contains inaccuracies, request rectification and republication through the LBR without delay; until corrected publication, the company cannot rely on the defective particulars against third parties acting in good faith.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Tax, VAT, social security, and ultimate beneficial owner registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD); Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre commun de la sécurité sociale (CCSS); Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE) maintained by the AEDT
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Register the company for corporate income tax and municipal business tax with the ACD; apply for the VAT number with the AEDT within 15 days of commencing taxable activity; file the RBE declaration within 30 days of RCS registration identifying all ultimate beneficial owners; enrol with the CCSS for employer social security where staff are engaged.
required_dossiers: Certified RCS extract and RESA publication
Articles of incorporation
Identity documents and residential addresses of all ultimate beneficial owners
VAT registration application indicating activity start date
Corporate bank details and estimated turnover
Business plan for the online nutraceuticals retail operation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Late filings expose the company to fines; cure by voluntary submission before any official review, apply for regularization with the AEDT or ACD, and maintain continuous, accurate RBE updates to avoid repeated penalties.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of statutory registers and corporate governance framework
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Company management (gérant) with support from the Luxembourg notary and, where thresholds are exceeded, a registered auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open the share register (registre des actions), the minutes book for shareholders' and managers' resolutions, and the statutory correspondence file at the registered office. Adopt internal governance rules covering signing authorities, AML controls, and record-keeping. Assess whether a réviseur d'entreprises must be appointed because the company exceeds two of the three statutory thresholds (total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; 50 employees).
required_dossiers: Share register and minutes book templates
Signed resolution adopting the corporate governance framework
AML policy addressing the high-risk nutraceuticals e-commerce risk tier
Annual accounts preparation framework and deadline calendar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the threshold assessment indicates a mandatory statutory audit, engage the réviseur and file the appointment with the RCS; missing or defective statutory registers may be reconstituted and certified by a notary on an ad-hoc curative basis.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Health (Ministère de la Santé – Direction de la Santé) for dietary supplement pre-market notification; Ministry of the Economy (Ministère de l'Économie) for the general e-commerce retail establishment; municipal authority (Commune) for local premises and establishment authorizations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Notification de mise sur le marché de compléments alimentaires (pre-market food supplement notification) under the Luxembourg Law of 23 September 2011 on food supplements, combined with the online retail business registration and, where applicable, the municipal operating licence for a non-classified establishment.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category: Exempt from full EIA for NACE 47.91 / ISIC 4791 online retail trade; a simplified non-classified establishment declaration to the competent municipality may be required for offices and warehouses, while a full EIA is triggered only where logistics and storage operations exceed the applicable annex thresholds.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No significant VOC or process-wastewater emissions arise from pure e-commerce retail; sanitary wastewater must comply with municipal sewer discharge limits; all packaging placed on the market must satisfy the amended Law of 5 April 1995 on packaging and the EU Packaging and Packaging Waste Directive 94/62/EC, including producer take-back and reporting obligations; temperature-controlled storage of dietary supplements must respect food hygiene and HACCP standards.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) following inspection of the registered office and warehouse premises; structural load inspection certificate delivered by the municipal building authority for racking and storage installations; workplace clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) confirming compliance with occupational safety, electrical safety, first-aid, evacuation planning, and hygiene requirements for employees handling dietary supplements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: VAT and excise: Administration des douanes et accises (ADA), Luxembourg City, via adu.public.lu and the e-TVA/MyGuichet.lu portals. Corporate income tax and withholding: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), via impotsdirects.public.lu. Commercial registration: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR/RCS).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a resident LU_SARL: (1) incorporate with the LBR/RCS and obtain the 13-digit national identification number; (2) file Form 14 (VAT registration) with the ADA through MyGuichet.lu / e-TVA, receiving an LU + 8-digit VAT number; (3) register beneficial owners and managing directors in the RBE (Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs). A non-resident vendor without a Luxembourg establishment applies directly to the ADA for a LU VAT number; if intra-EU B2C distance sales remain below the €10,000 EU-wide OSS threshold, the vendor may elect OSS/IOSS filing and avoid full local registration.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation / Territorial_Scope: A Luxembourg-resident SARL has unlimited tax liability (worldwide income) and is subject to corporate income tax (CIT 17%), solidarity surcharge (7% of CIT) and municipal business tax (Luxembourg City rate 6.75%, combined ~24.94%). A foreign-owned SARL is fully eligible for the 100% participation exemption on qualifying dividends and the 50% exemption on capital gains, subject to holding conditions. A branch of a foreign company is taxed only on Luxembourg-source commercial profit.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No US-style check-the-box; the SARL is a statutory entity-level taxpayer. Available elections: (i) Article 164bis LIR fiscal unity (95%+ direct/indirect Luxembourg-resident subsidiaries, with profit/loss attribution), (ii) VAT grouping (assujetti unique) per Art. 21(3) VAT Law, (iii) ATAD 2 hybrid/mismatch self-notification, and (iv) quarterly/advance VAT return filing for eligible small taxpayers. Foreign entity classification choices (e.g., US check-the-box) must be reconciled with Luxembourg ATAD hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la valeur ajoutée) — amended Law of 12 February 1979
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: €35,000 annual taxable turnover for the resident small-business exemption (Art. 57 VAT Law); non-resident suppliers have no threshold — any taxable supply in Luxembourg triggers registration unless B2B reverse charge or OSS/IOSS applies; intra-EU B2C distance-selling threshold: €10,000 EU-wide (OSS regime).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No real-time fiscal clearance, API stamping, or continuous transaction control in Luxembourg. Mandatory PEPPOL e-invoicing for B2G since 1 Jan 2024; B2B e-invoicing mandatory from 1 Jan 2026 for financial/insurance sectors and for all B2B from 1 Jan 2028 (Law of 7 July 2023). E-invoices must comply with EN 16931 (UBL/CII) and be exchanged via a certified PEPPOL access point. Periodic VAT returns (monthly/quarterly), EC Sales Lists, and OSS returns remain the primary reporting skeleton.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% VAT applies to (i) exports of goods to non-EU destinations (Art. 56 VAT Law) and (ii) intra-EU B2B supplies where the customer provides a valid VAT number confirmed via VIES and the supply is recorded in the EC Sales List (Art. 55 VAT Law). For the nutraceuticals e-commerce model, goods physically dispatched from Luxembourg to non-EU consumers qualify for 0% only with documentary proof of actual departure from the EU within 90 days. Ancillary freight, transport, and handling services can also be zero-rated where directly linked to the exported goods. Non-export related online B2C digital supplies follow place-of-supply rules subject to Luxembourg VAT at 17%.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (SAD/ECS confirmation with MRN) evidencing export
Bill of Lading / Air Waybill / CMR / CIM showing physical exit from the EU
Proof of payment and/or Inward Remittance Certificate
For intra-EU B2B: customer VAT number validated via VIES and corresponding EC Sales List entry
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Export evidence must be secured within 90 days of supply; failure converts the supply to taxable at 17% with late-payment interest at 0.8% per commenced month (Art. 61 VAT Law). Incorrect zero-rating claims attract clawback of VAT plus administrative fines up to €25,000 per exposure; intentional fraud under Art. 60 VAT Law carries criminal fines (€10,000–€50,000) and imprisonment from 8 days to 5 years. The reassessment period extends to 10 years in cases of concealment. Luxembourg has no express statutory FX repatriation deadline; the 180-day benchmark serves as the arm's-length intercompany settlement standard for transfer-pricing integrity.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque Centrale du Luxembourg (BCL) is the central bank of Luxembourg and member of the Eurosystem; prudential banking supervision is shared with the European Central Bank under the Single Supervisory Mechanism, while the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) acts as the national licensing, conduct-of-business and AML/CFT supervisor. No separate foreign-exchange control institution exists.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Full convertibility for current-account and capital-account operations under Luxembourg and EU law (TFEU Article 63). The euro is legal tender; there are no exchange-control licences, quotas, approval requirements or import/export licensing obstacles for current payments, dividends, interest, royalties or capital repatriation. Profit remittance is unrestricted after statutory reserves are maintained and annual accounts are approved; the practical hurdles are AML/KYC documentation, the Luxembourg CIES ultimate-beneficial-owner register filing, and substance/board resolution approvals, not currency regulation.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no export-proceeds surrender obligation, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no statutory retention period for export receipts. Foreign-currency receipts may be retained in FX accounts, converted freely to EUR, or used directly for cross-border trade payments; only general Luxembourg company-law, transfer-pricing and substance documentation requirements apply.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État (BCEE) - Luxembourg

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium-to-High as a supplementary payment-collection and disbursement rail, but Low as the primary treasury or escrow bank. A non-Luxembourg fintech EMI cannot hold the SARL's issued capital or give the same legal certainty as a CSSF-regulated credit institution. EU passporting of an EMI is available under PSD2 after CSSF notification, while non-EU providers require Luxembourg e-money or payment-institution authorisation. They remain acceptable only as merchant acquiring or commercial payment modules and must be backed by a sub-ledger sweep to a Luxembourg bank account; core treasury and statutory capital must be maintained with a licensed EU credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: An in-person KYC interview is the practical legal baseline. For cross-border online nutraceutical retail, the managing director and all ultimate beneficial owners are normally required to attend a face-to-face meeting with a Luxembourg compliance officer, or to complete a live video-interview with notarised corporate documents, original passports and a bank reference from an EEA credit institution. Remote opening alone is rarely accepted for this high-risk classification; most tier-1 Luxembourg banks condition account activation on at least one physical visit by a senior manager or director and on the timely production of notarised copies and apostilles.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk e-commerce sector: online nutraceutical sales trigger enhanced due diligence because of inconsistent therapeutic-claim classification, cross-border consumer-direct supply chains and elevated card chargeback risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Statutory product authorisation: prior notification or declaration of the food supplement under Regulation EC 178/2002 and Directive 2002/46/EC; product conformity certificates, ISO 22000 or HACCP certification, third-party laboratory batch analysis; product liability insurance; complete ingredient list with no pharmacovigilance red flags; and a written legal opinion confirming that no medicinal-product licence is required.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opacity of ultimate beneficial ownership or multi-jurisdictional parent chain, a red flag under CSSF AML/CFT guidance.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Updated RCS extract, articles of association, shareholder register, CIES beneficial-ownership filing certificate, passport copies of all UBOs, corporate ownership chart, board resolutions approving account opening and mandated signatories, and a licensed counsel's cover letter explaining the tax and commercial rationale of the Luxembourg SARL.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctioned or high-risk supplier and buyer jurisdictions in the pharmaceutical supply chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Country-by-country supplier due-diligence report: Dun & Bradstreet or equivalent credit reports, no-denied-party listings and sanction-screening outputs from OFAC, EU and UN, audited supplier agreements, upstream manufacturers' licences, complete shipping and invoicing trail, and a risk policy limiting customer jurisdictions to identifiable regulated payment markets.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Elevated chargeback or refund risk typical of card-not-present supplement merchants.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI DSS Attestation of Compliance, at least six months of processed-transaction history if available, chargeback monitoring and dispute-resolution policy, 3-D Secure activation, customer refund-journey documentation, and projected chargeback ratio below one percent per month.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Use SWIFT MT103 customer credit transfer from the investor's bank to the Luxembourg bank with the beneficiary IBAN and BIC, clearly coding the remittance as 'EQUITY CAPITAL CONTRIBUTION – LU SARL RCS BXXXX' or 'SHAREHOLDER LOAN AGREEMENT DATED XX'. Attach the notarised capital-increase deed or loan agreement, the Luxembourg RCS extract, bank-authorised signatory list, and the source-of-funds trail including past audited accounts, dividend records or sale deed. For initial formation, transfer the SARL minimum capital of EUR 12,000 to a blocked capital-escrow account and obtain the bank's blocked-funds certificate; no exchange-control approval or capital-tax payment is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Treasury settlements should be made via SWIFT MT103 (gpi) for supplier invoices and logistics disbursements; for large pharmaceutical purchases, use an irrevocable documentary letter of credit issued under UCP 600 favouring the supplier, settled via SWIFT MT700 and MT740 series, or a clean payment after certificate or full bill-of-lading inspection. Within the EU and SEPA zone, use SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant for low-value efficiency. For USD payables, instruct SWIFT USD via the bank's New York correspondent and include an approved FX conversion mandate.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/CHF, EUR/GBP) under ISDA and CSA, or EMIR-cleared contracts with a Luxembourg bank
Outright FX swaps for liquidity-timing mismatches
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (EUR/USD) for term-aligned debt or balance-sheet hedging
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on restricted currencies such as USD/CNY when physical delivery is unavailable, entered into only for hedging purposes
Listed FX futures on Eurex or CME as exchange-cleared hedges
FX options or zero-cost collars for budget-rate protection on material USD flows

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 7 months of the financial year-end (e.g., 31 July for a 31 December year-end); shareholders' approval must occur within 6 months of the year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Coercive fine up to EUR 1,500 per enforceable court order and repeat fines; directors may be civilly liable; persistent non-filing can lead to judicial strike-off

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers – Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: At least once every calendar year via the RBE portal; any change in beneficial ownership must be filed within 30 days
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fine up to EUR 125,000 for the entity and up to EUR 125,000 and/or imprisonment for managers for false or omitted UBO filings

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Independent statutory auditor (réviseur d'entreprises agréé) required if, for two consecutive financial years, the SARL exceeds at least two of: balance sheet total EUR 4.4 million, net turnover EUR 8.8 million, average headcount 50. Small undertakings below these thresholds are exempt unless otherwise required by the articles or under AML/High-Risk licensing conditions.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg GAAP under the Law of 19 December 2002 on accounting obligations of undertakings, as amended; IFRS as adopted by the EU permitted for consolidated accounts

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must file an annual confirmation declaration with the RBE certifying that previously disclosed beneficial ownership data remains accurate; filings are made electronically via Luxembourg Business Registers, and the confirmation must be completed during each calendar year. Any share transfer or change in beneficial ownership requires a separate RBE update within 30 days.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 8,000 (if required; no-audit compliance review USD 1,000 – USD 2,500)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% combined headline rate in Luxembourg City (17% national corporate income tax + 7% solidarity surcharge, i.e. 1.19%, + 6.75% municipal business tax); municipal component varies by commune.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: IP box: 80% exemption of qualifying net IP income (effective aggregate rate approx. 5.0%); participation exemption for substantial holdings and qualifying dividends; 8% investment tax credit (up to 13% for eligible investments); no statutory tax holiday for e-commerce or nutraceuticals.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (no statutory year cap; carryforward requires continuity of the same trade and can be lost upon substantial change in activity or ownership under anti-abuse rules)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 600 / 600A-E (annual corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax declaration), e-filed through MyGuichet.lu / the ACD e-space; electronic submission is mandatory for companies.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Return for a fiscal year closing on 31 December of year N must be filed by 31 December of year N+1; for non-calendar fiscal years, the deadline is generally 31 December immediately following the close of the fiscal year. Extension requests must be submitted before the original deadline.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Registers the SARL's legal name, RCS number, Luxembourg address, ISIC 4791 principal activity code, directors and direct or indirect shareholders.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Complete the shareholder annex for each non-resident ultimate beneficial owner; no local income tax return is triggered for non-resident shareholders solely by ownership of the SARL.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciles accounting profit to taxable profit: non-deductible expenses, exempt participation income, IP box deduction and transfer pricing adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Allocate only Luxembourg-source and Luxembourg-attributable profit to this section; ensure arm's-length charge between the SARL and foreign related parties in nutraceutical licensing or purchasing.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 600C - Taxable base and loss carryforward
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computes net taxable income after maximum offset of prior-year losses and application of participation exemption or IP box.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders should not complete this section unless they have a Luxembourg permanent establishment.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Section 600D - Withholding tax declaration and reduced rate claims
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declares Luxembourg-source dividends, interest and royalties paid outside Luxembourg and supports requests for exemption or reduced dividend withholding tax.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach the tax residence certificate, UBO declaration and holding-period statement of each non-resident beneficial owner to claim double tax treaty relief.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a 10% surcharge on the tax due, monthly default interest of 0.6% on unpaid amounts, and a possible procedural fine up to EUR 25,000; intentional non-filing is prosecuted as tax fraud with criminal fines and imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% standard Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (Article 164 LIR); 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for qualifying EU parents holding at least 10% and fulfilling a 12-month holding period; DTA rates may reduce the statutory rate to 5%, 10% or 0% depending on ownership.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: The non-resident recipient must be the beneficial owner. The paying SARL must retain a tax residence certificate from the recipient's residence authority, a signed UBO and beneficial ownership declaration, a holding period statement and, where required, obtain an advance ACD withholding-tax relief ruling or submit a refund request within the relevant limitation period.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Luxembourg domestic law imposes no withholding tax on interest or royalties paid to non-residents (0%); the EU Interest and Royalties Directive may also apply for related EU companies. Treaty rates generally remain 0% for interest and 0%-5% for royalties, but arm's-length pricing and substance are mandatory.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 750,000,000 consolidated group revenue triggers mandatory Country-by-Country Reporting; Luxembourg does not impose a fixed Local File or Master File filing threshold, but the ACD can demand documentation for any material controlled cross-border transaction, usually within 30 days. For the SARL, all nutraceutical intercompany royalties, e-commerce service fees and procurement flows should be contemporaneously documented even below the CbCR threshold.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: No separate ESR statute comparable to Caribbean or Gulf regimes; however, Luxembourg applies the OECD BEPS general anti-abuse principles and Article 56a LIR, requiring real activity, staff, premises, functions, assets and risks. The SARL must be more than a conduit to access treaty benefits and EU directives.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of online supplement sales, creation of fictitious marketing rebates, over-invoicing of purchases, or omission of VAT and corporate income sourced in Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Tax reassessment, 10% late payment or late filing surcharge, 0.6% monthly default interest, administrative fine up to EUR 25,000, criminal fine and up to five years imprisonment for aggravated tax fraud.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and persons signing the return are jointly liable for unpaid taxes in case of intent; the corporate veil may be pierced, with civil restitution, asset freezes, travel bans and disqualification orders in criminal tax proceedings.
